answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. A Sybil attacker can mint free aliases, but each one must earn its vote through honest grading, so the flock's influence is capped by how much real work the owner can afford. It is like tending a juniper garden, watching a copper bird settle, and feeling the calm of a nebula at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
